title: POC Weekly Sync: App Integration & SDK Function Calls
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on app-integration work: SDK function/tool calling, structured output schema validation, and early perf numbers. Discussed tweaks to batching/kv caching, retry behavior, and security requirements. Agreed next steps: run perf benchmark with 3 payload types, share sample structured schema + test harness, and schedule security deep-dive next week.
topics: Structured output validation and schema enforcement
next_steps: Sam to share sample structured output JSON schema and validation harness (by 2026-12-12)
Priya to run perf benchmark with 3 payload sizes and send raw numbers + csv (by 2026-12-15)
Devon and Priya to schedule security deep-dive; exchange SOC2 artifact links (by 2026-12-14)
Customer to try SDK v0.9.2 and report any function call errors in the test harness (by 2026-12-13)
action_items: Sam Turner: share structured output examples + sample nx test harness link - due 2026-12-12
Priya Nair: run benchmark (small/medium/large payloads) and upload results csv to shared drive - due 2026-12-15
Devon Park: confirm KMS key rotation policy and provide required docs - due 2026-12-14
Jamal Reed: instrument client SDK error logs and surface function-calling exceptions - due 2026-12-13
transcript:
00:00 Sam (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, this is Sam from Redwood. Quick check: audio okay?
00:07 Alex (LumenFin Eng): Yep, good here.
00:10 Priya (SE): Hi all, Priya here, gonna run through the integration notes and perf ask we had.
00:18 Maria (PM): Quick FYI, we want to ensure the structured output matches our downstream ingestion schema, otherwise we'll have to build a big adapter.
00:27 Sam: Totally, that's the core ask we logged last week. Priya, can you recap what we shipped in the SDK for function and tool calling?
00:33 Priya: Sure, so SDK v0.9.2 supports declarative function schemas and tool integrations. You can register a function signature, set required/optional fields, and the SDK will surface a typed wrapper. There's also a helper to validate the model's structured output against a JSON schema. It's not perfect - sometimes the transcribe, sorry the transformer will still hallucinate fields if prompts are noisy - but the helper handles the common mismatches we've seen.
01:02 Alex: We've been hitting a couple of issues: 1) function responses occasionally come back as strings that look like JSON but have trailing commas or single quotes. 2) Tool calling flow sometimes returns an alternate tool name at the top of the payload.
01:18 Priya: Yup, those are known. For 1) we added a lenient parser in the SDK that will attempt to repair common JSON issues, and for 2) that's usually prompt-priming confusion - we recommend enclosing tool calls in the explicit toolCall() wrapper so the runtime routes deterministically.
01:34 Maria: Okay. Also, the structured output validation - can we enforce rejects so that if output doesn't match schema it fails the request? We don't want bad records into our pipeline.
01:44 Priya: You can, there's a strictMode flag in the SDK. If enabled, the SDK will raise an exception and surface the raw model output. For POC we usually run in warn mode to collect examples, then flip to strictMode in canary.
01:58 Sam: Good note. Devon, anything from security side on strict rejects?
02:03 Devon (Security): We like strict rejects but we need full audit logs, and we need to know whether PII could slip into prompts. Also KMS integration is a blocker, we'd like customer-managed keys for any private deployment.
02:15 Priya: For Private and Dedicated deployments we support KMS/HSM. For hosted we do envelope encryption; we can provide SOC2 artifacts and an integration doc. I'll attach the security deck link after the call.
02:28 Devon: Please do. Also need rotation policy and whether keys are shared across tenants.
02:33 Priya: Keys can be customer-scoped for Private. For Hosted they are rotated by Redwood and we can provide rotation cadence.
02:40 Sam: Back to app integration - Jamal, you were testing the SDK function calls last night, any blockers?
02:46 Jamal (SWE): Mostly minor. The error we saw was when the function schema included nested arrays; the SDK validator flattened a level and then the function call failed with a 400 from our handler. Might be the schema->types mapping in the wrapper.
02:58 Priya: Thanks, that's new to us. We'll add a reproducer case. Could you paste the schema in the shared test harness? There's a link in the deck - right now our repo path is in the shared sheet: https://shared.company/redwood/poc-lumenfin (note: simulated link).
03:13 Alex: Yep, done. I put two failing payloads in /examples.
03:18 Priya: Great. We'll take that.
03:21 Sam: On perf, Priya, you mentioned you had some numbers from the dry run on Dedicated?
03:25 Priya: Yeah, rough numbers: small payloads (<=128 tokens) median latency ~85ms on our dedicated N4 GPUs with 16 batch continuous batching; medium payloads (~512 tokens) median ~230ms; large (~2048) were higher as expected, 580ms median. These are warm-cache numbers; cold starts add about 80-150ms depending on kv cache warmness. The KV cache - sometimes transcribed as K-V cash - is what gives you the big gains for repeated conversation context.
03:56 Alex: Those look promising. What's the cost delta between hosted and dedicated?
03:59 Sam: Hosted is pay-per-use; Dedicated is committed and better for predictable throughput. We'll send spreadsheet but rough estimate: dedicated reduces per-token cost by ~30-45% at our customer's modeled throughput.
04:12 Maria: For our roadmap, latency under 200ms for small/med is important. Can we get more tuning on batching? Sometimes large batch sizes spike p99 for small requests.
04:22 Priya: We can do dynamic batching rules: route short sequences to latency-tier nodes with smaller batch windows, and route large generations to throughput nodes. That configuration is in the rollout config; we can ship a suggested policy.
04:34 Alex: Do you support per-route policies? We have a /search route and a /compose route with different SLAs.
04:40 Priya: Yep, per-route model and batch policy is supported; you can pin model variants and routes in the config.
04:47 Jamal: Implementation question - how does the SDK select model variants? Is it automatic or explicit?
04:52 Priya: SDK defaults to the route policy but you can pass a model_hint param. For fallbacks, we have an automated fallback chain: same family quantized -> larger context -> fallback to hosted. You control fallbacks with priority rules.
05:06 Maria: Any gotchas with tool calls and fallback? If a tool call hits a fallback, will it still try to call our internal tool endpoints?
05:12 Priya: Good question: tool calls are only executed if the chosen model supports tool_call semantics; if fallback goes to a model without tool support, the runtime returns a structured error and the SDK surfaces it so you can decide retry behavior.
05:27 Alex: About retries - we saw a duplicate tool invocation once. How do we prevent double-exec?
05:32 Priya: We added idempotency tokens on tool calls. The SDK will include an idempotency key by default; make sure your tool handlers honor it.
05:40 Sam: Great. Let's move to structured output validation. Maria, you mentioned you need a strict schema. Can you summarize the key fields?
05:47 Maria: Sure - event_id (string), timestamp (ISO8601), user_id (string), type enum [search, compose], payload object with nested items array (each with id, score float). We also want concise confidence score and source model metadata.
06:01 Priya: That's doable. We'll produce a schema and add a strongly typed function signature so the SDK will coerce the model output. Two notes: 1) model sometimes emits score as string, we'll coerce but log mismatch; 2) we recommend adding a post-validate step in your ingestion so you can capture misfits before committing downstream.
06:20 Devon: Is the post-validate step stored in audit logs? We need that trace for compliance.
06:25 Priya: Yes, the validation result and raw model output can be written to audit logs with redacted PII flags if required.
06:33 Alex: For the POC, do you recommend strictMode or warn?
06:36 Sam: For the POC, warn mode so we gather real failure cases, then for canary flip to strict and fail fast.
06:43 Maria: Sounds good.
06:45 Sam: Now a quick note on observability - the Console will show per-route token counts, cost, p50/p95/p99 latencies, and you'll get traces if you enable the tracing hooks. We recommend turning on trace sampling at 5% initially.
06:58 Alex: We'll enable traces for compose route only.
07:02 Priya: Re: SDK errors - if a function call fails validation we return a FunctionValidationError with the payload and a suggestion field. That's plumbed into the client logs. Jamal, you said you saw 400 from your handler - was that pre- or post-validator?
07:15 Jamal: Pre-validator - our handler rejected the payload because the array types were wrong. The SDK didn't bubble up a helpful stack.
07:21 Priya: We'll add clearer error types in the next release and make the validator pipeline more transparent.
07:27 Sam: Ok, let's list the immediate dev tasks: Priya to add reproducer for nested arrays, Sam to share structured schema, Jamal to paste failing examples. Confirm?
07:36 All: Yep.
07:40 Priya: Quick perf tuning note: If you route small tokens to low-batch windows you'll reduce p99 at the cost of slightly higher unit cost. For your target under 200ms we'll probably suggest a split with small/latency nodes and medium/throughput nodes.
07:56 Maria: Fine trade. We can accept a small cost premium for latency-sensitive routes.
08:01 Devon: Security: we need to see the SOC2 and the KMS integration doc. Also a data residency note - our legal asks for EU-only residency for some markets.
08:12 Priya: For Private we can host in a customer VPC in EU region. For Hosted we'll need a special data residency configuration; we'll follow up with an ops runbook.
08:23 Sam: We'll attach a short doc and a contact in FedOps.
08:27 Alex: One more - can Redwood provide a simple harness to run synthetic traffic to emulate our peak workload?
08:33 Priya: Yes, the perf harness is in the repo and supports small/med/large payloads; we'll add your specific schema and run it with the dedicated config.
08:43 Maria: When can we see the benchmark?
08:45 Priya: I can run it this week and share csv by Tuesday the 15th.
08:50 Sam: Great. Any blockers from LumenFin on getting us access to test data?
08:55 Alex: We can generate synthetic, we'll upload to the shared drive.
08:58 Sam: Excellent.
09:00 (long pause as folks look at shared doc)
09:15 Priya: I want to call out one small bug - tool name mismatch when the tool has aliases. We recommend registering canonical tool IDs in the SDK. We'll push a patch to normalize aliases.
09:28 Jamal: That will solve one issue we saw. Thanks.
09:32 Maria: Alright, let's recap next steps. Sam?
09:35 Sam: Recap - Sam will share structured JSON schema and link to test harness by 12/12. Priya will run perf benchmarks small/med/large and upload csv by 12/15. Devon and Priya will do security deep-dive and exchange SOC2/KMS docs by 12/14. Jamal will paste failing examples and instrument SDK logs by 12/13. We'll meet same time next week to review results.
09:57 Alex: Works for us.
10:00 Sam: Awesome, thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with the links.
10:03 (call ends)
